title: Symmetric Mixed Equilibrium
body_html:
Symmetric Mixed Equilibrium

If a finite strategic game has a symmetry $\phi$, then it admits a mixed equilibrium $\sigma$ with the same symmetry: $$ \sigma=\phi(\sigma). $$
proof_html:
Sketch

Let $X$ be the closed convex subset of mixed profiles fixed by $\phi$. The uniform mixed profile lies in $X$, so $X$ is nonempty. Nash's fixed-point map respects the symmetry, hence maps $X$ to itself. Brouwer's fixed point theorem applied on $X$ gives a symmetric fixed point, which is a mixed equilibrium by Nash's argument.

References

  • [MFoGT, Thm. 4.6.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. A finite game with symmetry admits a mixed equilibrium with that symmetry.
